patch_description:
The previous best-performing variant (score 0.63) used parametrized CRZ gates with deliberate parameter sharing across topologically similar edges (e.g. (0,7)/(0,8) sharing "crz_2", (1,3)/(1,8) sharing "crz_3", (2,4)/(2,6) sharing "crz_4"), which both cut the parameter count and gave stronger entangling expressivity than fixed CZ gates. The current candidate regressed to fixed CZ gates on hub connections, which removed trainable phase information and increased circuit depth (59 vs 41) without any accuracy benefit (score dropped to 0.58). 

This edit reverts the fixed CZ gates back to parametrized CRZ gates that reuse existing parameter names from adjacent entangling gates (no new distinct parameters), restoring the expressivity that helped the 0.63-scoring version while keeping the parameter count essentially unchanged. It also converts the isolated CRX(3,5) gate to a CRZ (consistent rotation axis with the rest of the entangling layer, as in the top-performing variant) using its own dedicated parameter "crz_5", matching the proven design pattern. The disallowed-edge recommendation (1,2) is skipped since that pair is not in the allowed two-qubit wire list; instead we reinforce the already-validated shared-CRZ topology.
